“I should just say, I’ve been very lucky to have a lot of TV gigs, but this one’s really special,” Carson said on TODAY Nov. 5 after the announcement. “At my age and at my stage of my career, to have an opportunity to come in and sit next to Laura and to learn and to get better at my job to be the best broadcaster that I can, it’s not something I take lightly.”

title: Fan Fiction Site Archive of Our Own Is Down For Up to a Month. Can Fandoms Survive?
summary: The website AO3, or Archive of Our Own, is down for a month. Fan fic authors and its founder Rebeca Tushnet speak about the outage and what it means
story: There’s an often-memed joke in fandom and fan fiction spaces: “the AO3 author curse.” The superstition is defined on Urban Dictionary as “an occurrence in which a fan fiction author (typically writing on archiveofourown.org) gets into an extremely sticky situation, but said author’s first priority is their fan fic.” This might look like new installments being posted with notes like, “my beta reader is still in jail,” or “I was mugged.”

It’s impossible to assess the validity of these claims. Bela Rivas, a fanfic author from Sydney, Australia, can speak firsthand to her own experience: Her most popular fan fiction was finished and published from a hospital bed.

One morning at 4 a.m., she woke up feeling like she was drowning in blood. She was rushed to the hospital while vomiting blood and diagnosed with a hemorrhage, a complication from a recent tonsillectomy. Once she was stable, she returned to writing the “Buddie” (the ship name for Buck and Eddie from the ABC procedural drama “9-1-1”) story she had been working on.

“It was a way to think about anything other than the circumstances that I was in,” Rivas says. “Rather than sitting there and being worried, or rather than just spiraling, I think writing became for me such a way to deal with my own anxiety.”

The “author curse” is the butt of an internet joke. But the phrase belies what fan fiction and fandom can mean to its participants. Readers describe fan fic as an escape, a source of joy and community. Writers call it an accessible creative outlet or a way to process complex feelings.
So what happens when one of the platforms that makes it all possible goes dark?

Archive Of Our Own is currently experiencing its biggest outage ever since it launched to the public in November 2009, says Rebecca Tushnet, a founder of the Organization for Transformative Works, the non-profit behind AO3, and co-chair of its legal committee. On Oct. 29, the organization became aware of a “security problem” on AO3, Tushnet says, which is home to more than 18 million stories. No data from AO3 was deleted, the platform said in a statement. While it doesn’t believe the user database, which contains usernames, email addresses and IP addresses, was stolen, AO3 was “unable to rule it out.”
Finally, the devastating blow: “Our current expectation is that AO3 will be down for a minimum of two weeks; however, it could take up to four weeks.”
“It would be like if Netflix or HBO Max was to go down for two to four weeks,” AO3 user Brandon Frye, 26 of Columbus, Ohio, says.
What Happened to AO3?

On Oct. 29, Berklie Novak-Stolz, 29 of northern Alabama, had reached page 16 of the AO3 fan fics tagged to hurt/comfort, a popular fan fiction trope. When she reached the bottom of the page, she hit “next” and received a pop-up saying the archive was down for maintenance.

Temporary AO3 outages are common. The OTW has an X page for status updates with more than one million followers. At the time, maintenance was scheduled to take around 12 hours. No matter for Novak-Stolz, though. She just turned to her cache of saved fics. AO3 has a download feature, allowing readers to save fics in PDF, ePub and more formats.
Then she got a text from a coworker: “Did you see the news?” The question was accompanied by a screenshot of the status update that service restoration is expected to take two weeks.
That time estimation comes from exercising caution amid the “security incident,” which has not been explained further. The OTW has zero employees and is run by a team of about 1,000 volunteers.
“We are making sure that it is solved. This just requires being very careful and not bringing anything back until we’re confident it’s been patched,” Tushnet tells TODAY.com.
‘A Way For Me to Deal With Myself’

The internet, of course, reacted to the potential monthlong outage with memes. Frye posted a video of himself in a Halloween costume inspired by the AO3 outage, wearing pipe cleaners shaped like the site’s logo as a headband and papers that read “Error 404” and “Not Found.”

“I initially was like, ‘Two to four weeks is a very, very long time,’” Novak-Stolz says. “I know that for a lot of people, myself included, fan fic is like a really good escape, especially because the world’s like an on fire dumpster at the moment. These are my silly little stories.”
The outage has also reminded readers that it’s more than that.

“One of the best things about fandom is it has a very low barrier to entry, and you can find people who like the same things you do and are interested in helping you become a better storyteller,” Tushnet says.
Novak-Stolz recalls that after the death of her brother four years ago, she turned to reading and writing fan fiction, often about the characters from “Supernatural.”
"I'm really good at being able to sit down and think, 'This character's mad, but why? What's the root of that?' ... It's a way for me to deal with myself, too."
Bela Rivas AO3 fan fiction writer
“The kindness from strangers on the internet is what helped me get through that time,” she says.
Right after he passed, she says she spent 16 hours reading on the site in one day. Now, she clocks in around two to three hours of screen time on the site per day.
“I didn’t want to be alone with my thoughts, so I was like, let me put someone else’s thoughts in my head,” she says.
“For a lot of people, it’s just like a place separate from everything else,” she adds.

Rivas started writing fan fiction as an adult in 2021 after breaking up with her longterm boyfriend and coming out as queer. After her dog had surgery, she spent most nights sleeping on the floor downstairs with him and rewatched “Teen Wolf,” inspiring her first stories. She’s also written for “Supernatural” and most popularly, for “9-1-1,” an ABC procedural about first responders that’s currently airing its 10th season.
Many of her 60-plus published fan fics are coming-out stories. She says they allow her to process her own experience through characters she can connect with.

It also allows her to delve into material from the canon that feels unexplored. For example, firefighter Eddie Diaz, one half of one of AO3’s most popular new ships, is not canonically queer in the show “9-1-1.” But he is canonically struggling with what masculinity looks like and dating feeling like performance, Rivas says. He’s also Latino and dealing with religious guilt — “that’s very me,” Rivas says.

“There are metaphors that I’ve used repeatedly because they’re how it felt for me,” Rivas says. “I’ve had Eddie Diaz in different fics talk about there being a door in his head, and he kept shutting it. ... And one day it opened a little bit further and he couldn’t close it again, and when the door opened, it was actually just sunshine. He’d spent so long in the dark.”
‘We Are Going to Get Through This Together’

When AO3 has temporarily gone down in the past, Novak-Stolz has posted about it on TikTok to her more than 300,000 followers. This time, she did something different. Her Oct. 29 video opened with a meme from “Supernatural” alongside the outage announcement. She was in the middle of making the video when she thought of creating a public Google Drive for people to upload their own collections of downloaded fan fictions.
“You know what, we are going to get through this together as a community with the power of friendship and mutual aid,” she said in the video.

“I stopped mid video, created the Drive, put the link for it in my LinkTree, and then finished the video,” she tells TODAY.com. “I actually haven’t been able to upload any of the fics I have saved because it exploded so fast.”

Direct clicks from her LinkTree alone number more than 250,000, she says. Links to her Drive could also be found across social media comments sections. On Election Day, Nov. 3, the official TikTok account for the Democratic party posted a photo edit of her Drive, which was titled “Fanfic Emergency Fund,” with the caption, “streets are saying if you vote blue AO3 will come back.”

But the act of uploading content from AO3 in other online spaces has come with backlash. In Novak-Stolz’s own Drive, she initially had permissions set that allowed everyone to be an editor, and she says some bad actors uploaded potentially dangerous links. And in addition to fan fic Google Drives, sites masquerading as AO3 have cropped up, claiming to be a re-creation of the platform’s content. Some users have reportedly encountered sites claiming to sell audiobook versions of fan fics.

When Rivas first heard of the plan for collective sharing of downloaded fan fics, she was initially “completely in favor of it.” She then heard counterarguments from other authors who didn’t want their content uploaded to Drive, citing the site’s lack of content warnings and the possibility of data being scraped by AI.
“I think that people who don’t want it should be respected,” Rivas says, later adding that she believes the “liabilities, both morally and legally, are just too high.”

Asked for the OTW’s stance on the republishing of fan fictions into places like Google Drive, Tushnet says AO3 authors have copyright over any original material they contribute when writing a fan fiction. The OTW primarily focuses on preventing the monetization of fan fiction. But with the site down, some authors “just want to know where their things are, and we think that is completely reasonable,” Tushnet says.
“There is a difference between saving something for yourself and then putting it online for the entire world to see, and we hope people will be respectful of authors’ wishes,” Tushnet says.
Both Novak-Stolz and Rivas have received extreme backlash and harassment on social media.

Novak-Stolz’s initial Drive is now defunct, but she and 30 other people built a new one with an organizational system and altered permission settings. She says she’s spoken directly with authors who didn’t want their work in the Drive, and there’s a process in place to remove them.
Novak-Stolz says she’s been told she should delete her account and quoted a hate comment she received that mentioned her brother’s death. Still, she says she doesn’t regret making the Drive.

“Because I know how important it is to have these communities, because I would not have made it through any of the bad, truly terrible times of my life without these communities, without these works, without these like, silly little fictional guys,” she says. “But also the opposition for it, it’s kept me up at night.”

Meanwhile, when Rivas posted on X about the hate authors who have criticized uploading their work elsewhere are receiving, she says she received comments telling her to delete everything and “no one will miss you.”

“When the outage first happened ... there was this idea of like, ‘Oh, we’re going to try and get so much done in this time so we have heaps to post when it comes back,” Rivas says. “And then it pretty abruptly turned into, ‘Wow, I’m feeling so dehumanized by this and I’m feeling so demotivated to write.’

“Now I’m seeing a lot of people I know who’ve been writing for years saying, ‘I don’t know if I’m going to continue doing this because this sense of connection that I had feels like it’s gone,’” she adds.

She says she’s not giving up on that sense of community, and she won’t stop posting stories. Through writing fan fiction she’s become best friends with people across the world and grown more secure in her sense of self and her abilities.

“There is that community,” she says. “I really believe in that and I really want that to stay, and I hope that that isn’t something that’s too damaged by this. I hope that there’s a middle ground to be found in understanding that we’re not coming from a place of disrespecting readers either, or not wanting to share with them.
“Of course I want readers to read what I wrote, why else would I have written it?” she adds. “But I also don’t want to be disconnected from it.

“The most popular fic I’ve ever written was written during one of the scariest and worst periods of my life, and the idea that people take it and say, ‘This isn’t even yours anymore because you published it. This doesn’t connect to you. This is mine. I own it. I can do whatever I want with it.’ It’s like, I guess you can. I can’t stop you, but how sad?”
Tushnet says OTW’s primary concern at this time is protecting users from scammers and emphasizing internet safety. She advises users to be “extremely careful” with any links they click on.

“When you’re upset and worried is when you’re most vulnerable, and scammers no that,” Tushnet says. “We just hope people will give us a little bit of time. There was no data lost. It’s all coming back. Just hang on.”

title: The 2026 Rockefeller Center Christmas Tree Officially Arrives at the Plaza After a 200-Mile Journey
summary: After a four-hour journey from upstate New York, this year’s Rockefeller Center Christmas Tree has finally arrived at the Plaza.
story: What an unbeleafable sight!
After a four-hour journey from upstate New York, this year’s Rockefeller Center Christmas Tree has finally arrived at the Plaza.
And she’s marvelous!

“I’m always amazed at the massive crowd that shows up here. Hundreds of people to give the tree a good New York welcome,” said Saturday TODAY’s Joe Fryer, who was on board with the spruce as it entered the Plaza. “It’s like a parade with one float, and this beautiful Norway spruce is the Grand Marshal.”
The Norway Spruce, which stands at a whopping 76 feet and weighs 11 tons, hails from the rural hamlet of West Edmeston.
Its trek to midtown Manhattan involved a ride in a 100-foot-long trailer.
After its arrival, the tree is then lifted off the trailer by a crane, suspended in mid-air, and then carefully positioned into its spot.

The spruce, donated by owner Rebecca Decker, has been growing for more than seven decades. Rockefeller Center head gardener Erik Pauze, who’s tasked with finding the Christmas tree each year, told TODAY he first spotted the tree six years ago. Its shape was what really what sold him.
“I knew it was perfect,” Pauze said.
Pauze contacted Decker a few years later, and the tree owner was shocked.
“Erik actually came and knocked on the door and said, ‘That’s a really nice tree,’” Decker recalled. “And I thought that he was absolutely joking.”
Decker, who said that she “never once” thought that her tree would carry the mantle of the Rockefeller Center Christmas Tree, says she initially believed that the ask “was fake at first.”
“She did look at me kinda funny,” Pauze said of that early interaction.
Now, Decker says she appreciates the tree’s beauty even more. And might actually have a bit of trouble parting with it.
“I’m actually a little sad to see it leave now,” she told Joe. “Now I don’t really know how the yard’s going to look without it.”
Still, the mom of three is stoked to witness her tree’s New York City debut with her family.
“To me, it’s pretty big,” she said. “I am super excited for them to be able to experience this.”

With the tree officially in its new home, the spruce will now undergo weeks of decorating. The makeover will consist of more than 50,000 multi-colored LED lights, along with a 900-pound Swarovski star, dripping in three million crystals.
By Dec. 2, the spruce will be all dolled up for the tree lighting ceremony.

title: ‘I Play Rocky’ Star Anthony Ippolito Shares His Official Ranking of ‘Rocky’ Franchise Movies
summary: Anthony Ippolito, the star of “I Play Rocky” and deadringer for Sylvester Stallone, has hit us with his official ranking of the “Rocky” movie franchise.
story: Anthony Ippolito, the star of “I Play Rocky” and deadringer for Sylvester Stallone, has hit us with his official ranking of the “Rocky” movie franchise. And it’s a knockout.

Ippolito, who stopped by TODAY Nov. 5 to talk about the new film, which is already getting Oscar buzz, tells TODAY.com that of the six “Rocky”-centered movies, the original 1976 film, of course, tops the list.
“The first one is first,” Ippolito says. “I’d probably put ‘Rocky Balboa’ second, the sixth one. Then maybe ‘Rocky II.’”

Ippolito’s new film — which was released Nov. 6 in select theaters and will be headed for nationwide release later this month — peels back the curtain on the making of Stallone’s 1976 sports classic, taking viewers inside Sly’s personal story of struggle and tenacity while attempting to get his underdog movie made.

Audiences are well aware that the movie eventually became a franchise that not only included six “Rocky” films, but also three others focused on the fictional Apollo Creed, Rocky’s rival-turned-valued friend. But they’re less acquainted with Stallone’s story prior to his fame and fortune — one that, the movie shows, mirrors Rocky Balboa’s journey in spirit.
Ippolito, who plays Stallone in the film, underwent extensive prep for the role, including some long conversations with Sly himself. So we’d say that his ranking is pretty darn official.
His full ranking of the six films are as follows:
“Rocky,” 1976
“Rocky Balboa,” 2006
“Rocky II,” 1979
“Rocky IV,” 1985
“Rocky III,” 1982
“Rocky V,” 1990
Solid.

Ippolito, who had barely any prior boxing experience, shares with TODAY.com that he trained for the boxing scenes at the legendary Gleason’s Gym in Brooklyn, the oldest active boxing gym in the U.S. that served as training grounds for a number of champions including late greats Muhammad Ali and Jake LaMotta.
So, you know Ippolito has got a great training montage queued up in his head for when it’s go-time.
The 27-year-old actor, who put on 30-40 pounds for the role, says that he even has the perfect training montage theme song: “Walk,” the 1992 single from heavy metal band Pantera.
“There’s just nothing like it,” Ippolito says, lighting up.

title: Willard Scott Is Kissed By Barbara Bush at Inauguration in 1989
summary: First lady Barbara Bush kissed Willard Scott on the lips during the inauguration of her husband, President George H. W. Bush, in 1989.
story: As TODAY marks its 75th anniversary, the TODAY Archive is revisiting legendary interviews, stories that moved us and other iconic moments from our 75 years on the air. These are the segments that shaped TODAY and created a lasting legacy. Today, we look back at Willard Scott getting a smooch from Barbara Bush during the presidential inauguration on Jan. 20, 1989.
George H.W. Bush won the presidential election in 1988 and his inauguration, on Jan. 20, 1989, turned into an unforgettable moment for one TODAY personality.

Willard Scott was on the ground for the inauguration in Washington, D.C., for TODAY and wound up getting a peck on the lips from first lady Barbara Bush while she and her husband walked along the parade route.
Willard Scott Spotted the President
“The president is appearing as you can see him right now,” Scott said, as George H.W. Bush and his wife walked.
The president waved as the throngs of people cheered.
“Mr. President, bless your heart, do we love you!” exclaimed Scott, as he walked by and appeared to say “thank you” to Scott — or at least someone in his direction.
Barbara Bush Races Over to Kiss Willard Scott
At that moment, Barbara Bush, clad in a teal, button-down winter coat, jogged over to the TODAY weatherman and gave him a quick kiss on the lips before she raced back to the parade route.
“Thank you,” Scott said.
“How ‘bout that? I’ve been kissed by the best,” he continued with a chuckle. “I got kissed off by the president, but I got kissed by the first lady.”
The Kiss Stayed With the First Lady
Barbara Bush died in 2018 at the age of 92, while Scott died in 2021 at the age of 87. That moment with the first lady remained a delightful encounter for all involved.
“I think it was one of her life highlights,” Bush’s granddaughter Jenna Bush Hager said on TODAY a few days after Scott’s death.

“I emailed somebody that worked with her and she said, ‘You know, they just really liked each other,’” she continued. “They said there was some sort of chemistry there where she said, ‘I feel like they were flirting,’ and obviously we have the proof.”

title: Carson Daly Shares How He’s Feeling Ahead of New Saturday TODAY Gig: ‘Overwhelmed, But Mostly Incredibly Grateful’
summary: Carson Daly is opening up about how is feeling a day before he begins a “new chapter” at TODAY as the Saturday edition co-host with Laura Jarrett.
story: Carson Daly is opening up about how is feeling a day before he begins a “new chapter” at TODAY.

It was announced Nov. 5 that Carson will permanently join Laura Jarrett as co-anchor of Saturday TODAY. Ahead of his first weekend episode, which will air Nov. 7, he shared a post on Instagram about his new role and revealed the gift he seemingly received from TODAY co-anchor Savannah Guthrie.

“Maybe slightly overwhelmed, but mostly incredibly grateful for all the well wishes & kind thoughts for my new Sat @todayshow gig,” he wrote in his caption. “A new chapter, a new challenge, and a new opportunity to get better at what I love to do. I’m ready for it.”
He added that the support he has received from members of the NBC News family since the announcement was made has meant a lot to him.
“I hope to do you proud. It’ll be a process, gotta lot to learn & it all starts live tomorrow am with my partner @laurajarrett Cya then!” he said and included a tongue-out emoji.
The post included a picture of a bottle of Blanton’s bourbon whisky and a handwritten note seemingly from Savannah. “For the Anchorman. So proud. Love Savannah,” she said.
Other members of the TODAY and NBC News family wished him well in the comments.
Laura wrote, “So many good times ahead—bourbon, gummies and Levain included.”
Vicky Nguyen added, “Bring it home for our generation Carson! The one constant in everyone’s life- Carson Daly on a TV broadcast … now almost daily!”
Former NBC News correspondent Janet Shamlian said, “This is what my Saturday morning has been missing, @carsondaly.”
Shop TODAY’s Adrianna Brach commented, “Bonbon and Blanton’s!! You got this @carsondaly !!!!”

Carson had been appearing as an interim co-anchor on Saturday TODAY with Laura since September. When he revealed earlier this week he would officially become her co-anchor, he confirmed he will still be a part of TODAY’s regular weekday broadcasts.

“I should just say, I’ve been very lucky to have a lot of TV gigs, but this one’s really special,” he said after making the announcement. “At my age and at my stage of my career, to have an opportunity to come in and sit next to Laura and to learn and to get better at my job, to be the best broadcaster that I can, it’s not something I take lightly.”
Along with Laura, Carson will join feature anchor Joe Fryer and meteorologist Angie Lassman, as well.

Carson continued, “We’re going to have a lot of fun on Saturday. But most importantly, the best part about the gig, like here during the week — which I’ll still be here during the week — is getting to go to your place of employment with such high-quality human beings. We are a family, and the fact that I get to spend one more day in this building, six days a week, is an absolute honor.”

To celebrate, the TODAY family shared a Guinness toast. Savannah also praised Carson for making “every segment he’s in pop” and shared he is “like a brother” to her. “You bring so much love and light, and I am so happy,” she said when reacting to his new position.
Laura added, “We’re going to have so much fun.”
Carson replaces Peter Alexander, who left the show in March and departed NBC News after 22 years. He is currently a host at MS NOW.
Carson has been with TODAY since 2013. He delights viewers each episode with his pop culture and celebrity news during the PopStart segment.
Carson is permanently joining Laura Jarrett as a co-anchor on the weekend show starting Nov. 7.

title: Knicks Show Their Support for Taylor Swift After Player Calls Her Fakest Celeb Fan
summary: A Knicks spokesperson released a statement after point guard Tyler Kolek named Taylor Swift the fakest celebrity fan at their games.
story: The Knicks are expressing their support and appreciation for Taylor Swift after a couple of players called her reactions at their games “performative.”
While appearing on NBA 2K League’s “Deflected” video series, Tyler Kolek and Deuce McBride were asked who they thought was the “fakest celebrity fan” they’ve seen sitting courtside at an NBA game.

“At the Knicks game, I would say it’s very performative ‘cause they just want to be seen at the game. They’re not necessarily fans,” Kolek said in the video published Nov. 5, before answering, “Maybe Taylor Swift?”
McBride added, “I would agree.”
Kolek questioned if he had “seen her at any other games,” while noting that he “might get some hate” from Swifties.
McBride then named some “solid” celebrity fans who he’s regularly spotted at the games, like Ben Stiller and Tracy Morgan.
Kolek did mention Swift’s busy schedule, saying, “So she can’t come all the time.” However, he added, “It’s a little performative.”
Following the comments and backlash online, a spokesperson for the Knicks defended the superstar.

“Taylor Swift has been a Knicks fan for many years, has a long history with Madison Square Garden, and we are incredibly appreciative of her support of the organization,” the statement shared with TODAY.com on Nov. 6 reads.
TODAY.com reached out to Kolek and McBride for additional comment.

Earlier this year, Swift, along with Este Haim and Mariska Hargitay, was seen sitting courtside in a black and orange tee, supporting the Knicks during the finals. She also attended a Knicks game with now-husband Travis Kelce, and they got married at Madison Square Garden.
Photos of the “Patient Zero” singer at Knicks games date back to 2014, with one game sitting next to Stiller.
Swifties, however, are familiar with Swift’s enthusiasm during sports games, as well as awards shows.
Swift can usually be seen dancing and cheering on her friends and artists she admires at events, as well as Kelce and his Kansas City Chiefs team during their NFL games.

title: ‘Golden Bachelorette’ Stars Joan Vassos and Chock Chapple End Engagement After 2 Years
summary: “The Golden Bachelorette” stars Joan Vassos and Chock Chapple have announced the end of their engagement after two years together.
story: “The Golden Bachelorette” stars Joan Vassos and Chock Chapple have announced the end of their engagement after two years together.
The two, who met on the first season of the ABC reality dating series, released identical statements on their Instagram stories on Friday, Nov. 6, confirming their breakup.

“Two years ago, Chock and I took a leap of faith and got engaged during our season of The Golden Bachelorette, hoping we had found our forever. We spent the last two years living what we hoped would be the beginning of our love story, sharing our families, amazing adventures, laughter, and supporting each other through challenging times,” Vassos wrote in the statement uploaded to her page. “Sadly, our journey hasn’t turned out the way we had hoped and we have decided to end our engagement.”
She added, “We truly want each other to be happy, and I’m grateful for the chapter we shared.”

Vassos and Chapple had instant chemistry on her season of “The Golden Bachelorette.” He briefly departed the show when his mother passed away but later returned to continue his relationship with Vassos. In the season finale, which aired in November 2024, he met her children and declared his love for her.

On proposal day, he acknowledged their late partners in his speech, including Vassos’ husband John who died of pancreatic cancer in 2021. Chapple said he planned to “honor” John by “loving her every day.”
Vassos told him, “We are living proof that no matter what life throws at you, there is still hope, even at our age,” before sharing that she loved him.
He proposed and Vassos handed him her final golden rose.

For the past two years, they have been keeping fans updated on their long-distance relationship with frequent social media posts. They also appeared together in an Inspire commercial about Chapple using the company’s sleep apnea device.
But in August, the two revealed that they were going through a challenging time due to health struggles.

In a joint video uploaded to Instagram, Chapple shared that after filming ended he had a blood test that revealed elevated prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels. He said the levels continued to increase and turned “aggressive,” so he had two biopsies and an MRI.
“Last Wednesday I had my prostate removed,” he shared, with Vassos by his side. “I have cancer in my family. I lost my mother to cancer and I thought this was the best thing.”
He said recovery had been “a little rough.”
“I’ve had a number of surgeries, this one’s a little unique,” he continued. “But glad I had it done. Joan’s been here taking care of me.”
She chimed in and praised Chapple for how he handled his health issues.
“This one was a little harder so he’s been really brave. He’s actually a really good patient,” she complimented. She also said the two planned to take a trip to Europe at the end of the month.
After the Bachelor Nation Instagram account posted about their split, alums weighed in.
Sandra Mason, who appeared with Vassos on Season 1 of “The Golden Bachelor,” commented, “Love them both. Hope they continue a beautiful friendship.”
“The Golden Bachelorette” Season 1 star Jonathan Rone said, “Really respected how you both opened your hearts and shared your journey with us! Wishing you both peace and happiness ahead.”

title: At 9, He Was Banned From Delta for Pulling a Prank. Now He’s the Voice of Boston’s Logan Airport
summary: Arlington pipefitter Chris Donisi beat nearly 6,000 hopefuls to become the Voice of Logan Airport. His mom made him enter, and she called it from day one.
story: Somewhere over the Eastern Seaboard in the early 1990s, a 9-year-old boy flying alone discovered the flight attendant call button.
He pressed it. A flight attendant appeared. He switched the light off. He pressed it again.

“I did it probably like 15 times,” Chris Donisi tells TODAY.com. When the plane landed in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, the captain came out, took back the little plastic wings he’d been given and told him he would never fly Delta again. His aunt Phyllis saw all of it, and she marched him to the car by his ear.

That was Donisi’s first real memory of Boston Logan International Airport. His next one will have a much bigger audience. Starting this month, roughly 43 million travelers a year will hear him welcoming them home.

On Nov. 5, the Massachusetts Port Authority named Donisi, 43, the first “Voice of Logan.” He is a pipefitter from East Arlington. The two-month contest drew nearly 6,000 audition videos and about 35,000 public votes. Massport’s chief executive, Rich Davey, broke the news live on Kiss 108’s “Billy & Lisa in the Morning.” He later introduced Donisi at a news conference at the airport as “a pipefitter with pipes.”
The gig is unpaid. Donisi is keeping his day job.
‘Ma, All Right’

Massport launched the contest in September. Entrants, all Massachusetts residents, read a short welcome script. The search became a local sensation. It inspired reader-submitted scripts, an open casting call in Terminal A and, on Jimmy Kimmel’s show, an audition from Ben Affleck.

Donisi almost didn’t enter. His mother, Helen Donisi, 70, found the opportunity and sent it to him. Weeks went by. With three or four days left before the deadline, she asked whether he’d recorded his video.
He hadn’t.
“She got mad and she told me, ‘Just do it, please do it,’” he says. “And I said, ‘Ma, all right, I’m gonna do a quick one.’” He went downstairs, did a couple of takes and hit send.
“It’s an I-told-you-so story,” he says.
When the eight finalists were narrowed to one, Donisi had no idea. He’d received an email about a media training session. He assumed he was logging on to a group Zoom with the other contestants.

Instead, he found Kiss 108 and Davey waiting for him. “It was a deer in headlights moment,” he says. “The emotions just flooded, and it was just all good things and just excitement, overwhelmed, but in a good way.”
What won him the job, of course, was the voice, and Donisi has thoughts on what makes it so Boston.
To most out-of-towners, a Boston accent is a Boston accent. Donisi hears it differently. Locals, he says, can often place a speaker down to the neighborhood or town just by listening.

“People, they’ll call you up. They say, ‘Hey, you from Somerville? Are you from Charlestown? You from Arlington?’” he says. “It’s almost like people can point out the accent to a specific town or area.”
He argues it isn’t really about the dropped R’s.
“It’s about the flow of the accent,” he says. “It really, really changes neighborhood to neighborhood. It’s just the way people kind of, you know, dance when they talk.”

The accent appears to be getting passed down. Donisi and his wife, Kristin, have two children: Freya, 3, and Odin, 2. Kristin is a nurse and is also from Arlington. Odin is still mostly at “dada.” Freya, he says, is “definitely grasping it.”
Some people are from Boston. Others seem to have been built by it. Donisi is firmly in the second camp, and his answers to a few quick-fire questions make the case.
The Lightning Round
Most Boston thing he’s ever done: riding the T all night as a kid.
Favorite team: The Bruins, “all day.” The Patriots, Red Sox and Celtics are loved, too, but “when it comes down to brass tacks,” the Donisis are hockey people.
Dunkin’ order: a medium regular with a Boston cream. Sometimes hash browns.
Go-to restaurant: Caffe Paradiso in the North End.
Celebrity he’d pick to introduce him over the loudspeaker: Ben Affleck. “After I saw him do the Voice of Logan thing,” he says, “that’d have to be him.”

What Boston means to him: “Boston is my heart for sure,” he says. “Boston made me who I am and how I work.” Over 43 years, he says, he has watched the city’s highs and lows and the way people rally around each other, “even with this competition.”
That includes his fellow finalists, whom he calls winners, too. The group has been texting since the news broke. They are trying to get together to celebrate.
Massport says Donisi will begin recording soon, so his messages can be playing by mid-November, in time for the holiday rush.

title: Martha Stewart Sits Down With Craig Melvin to Address Halloween Costume Controversy
summary: During the Nov. 6 TODAY episode, Martha Stewart addressed the backlash she received following her controversial Halloween costume.
story: Martha Stewart apologized on TODAY following her controversial Halloween costume that appeared to depict a homeless person and said Craig Melvin was not at fault for her wearing the outfit that sparked a backlash.

The 85-year-old lifestyle guru has been facing criticism since she posted a now-deleted photo of her looking disheveled while holding a clipboard that read, “I AM HUNGRY HELP ME!!” for Halloween, per NBC News. During her appearance on TODAY Nov. 6, Stewart addressed the controversy and how Craig got roped into it.

“I made a mistake,” Stewart said. “I was stupid, what else can I say? I am so sorry, and I hope that my followers and my fans and the rest of America forgives me for doing something that was not meant in any way to be a bad thing.”

Craig then asked Stewart about reports that said she claimed she wore the last-minute costume because he spilled chocolate on her sweater during their TODAY Halloween special segment on Oct. 30, where Craig was dressed as rapper Snoop Dogg.
“I didn’t have a costume because you had spilled some chocolate on my white sweater, and I don’t blame you at all,” she told Craig. “It was a joke that I said I blamed you. It was stupid.”
Stewart said she was giving a talk and made a joke that Craig had spilled chocolate on her so she couldn’t wear that costume and pivoted to the other one instead.
“Of course, they picked up on that because you’re you,” Stewart said.
“But I did apologize for spilling the chocolate,” Craig said. “We moved on.”
“And it wasn’t your fault,” Stewart said.
She also shared feedback she received from her family.

“Tone-deaf, or whatever I was. According to my grandson, I was tone-deaf,” she said. “He saw the picture first because I sent it to him and I said, ‘What do you think?’ ‘Tone-deaf,’ he said. It was just stupid, and I apologize because I was not making fun of anybody or making light of the great problems that face our country.”
Stewart, who will return to TODAY next week for the annual All-Star Thanksgiving segment, shared what she learned from the controversy.
“Pay closer attention to social issues,” she said. “Be aware. I’m aware of all those social issues, as you can imagine, and I care desperately about all the problems facing us.”

For her Halloween costume, Stewart wore torn clothing and covered her face in makeup to resemble dirt. Her Instagram post with a picture of the costume doubled as an ad for her candle collection on QVC. “My QVC candles are perfect for Halloween!!!” she captioned the since-deleted post.
After some criticized the costume for being “out of touch” and “dystopian,” according to NBC News, Stewart reacted to the negative responses in a statement.

“I am distressed that my Halloween costume yesterday, which was intended to bring more awareness to the very serious subject of homelessness, has offended people, which was never my intention,” she said in a statement to NBC News on Nov. 1.

Homelessness, she wrote, “continues to remain one of America’s greatest challenges and ongoing crises, something that I care deeply about and I have spent a significant amount of time and effort supporting charities that combat this ongoing social epidemic.”
At the end of her statement, Stewart added, “I am committed to continuing to make a difference.”
Stewart then penned a second statement that she shared on her Instagram page on Nov. 1, as well.

“It’s hard to admit when you’ve really screwed up. My earlier statement didn’t go far enough. I know many people are suffering economically. Wearing a costume like I did was insensitive and not funny. I am very sorry,” she wrote.
The post has since been deleted.

title: Jalen Brunson’s ‘Law & Order: SVU’ Cameo Has a Playful Reference to the Knicks’ Big Win: ‘Gave It 110%’
summary: Mariska Hargitay’s dreams of a Jalen Brunson guest appearance on “Law & Order: Special Victims Unit” have become a reality.
story: Mariska Hargitay’s dreams of a Jalen Brunson guest appearance on “Law & Order: Special Victims Unit” have become a reality.

In August, the actor appeared on TODAY saying she was manifesting a cameo from the New York Knicks captain. Now, fans of the NBC series can watch the basketball player flex his acting muscles in the latest episode.
Brunson plays a character named Detective Madison in an episode titled “Forsaken,” which airs on NBC Nov. 5 at 9 p.m. ET. It will also stream on Peacock the next day.

The Knicks player appears in one scene and assists Olivia Benson (Hargitay) with an investigation. When the two meet at a coffee shop, Benson greets her colleague by saying, “Detective Madison, look at you out of uniform, huh? Congratulations on the promotion.”
Brunson’s response appears to contain a cheeky reference to his team’s recent championship run.
“Thanks captain. Focused on my goals, gave it 110 %. Things worked out,” he says.
“Yeah, they did,” Benson replies.
The two briefly discuss an assault investigation then Benson is on her way as she makes a phone call.
“Thanks Jay, you’re the best,” she says as she pats him on the back.
Hargitay, a die-hard Knicks fan, visited Studio 1A over the summer and hinted at a potential collaboration with Brunson.
“And I’m hoping that we might — don’t tell anyone, but — see (Brunson) on ‘SVU,’” she told TODAY’s Savannah Guthrie.

The following month, the official “Law and Order” Instagram page posted a video of Brunson saying he wanted to “try to get on ‘SVU.’” In the next slide, they shared a photo of the athlete with the cast of the show.
“When the plans finally make it out of the group chat 🤌 Jalen Brunson is officially headed to #SVU!” the caption read.

While promoting the upcoming season premiere of “Law and Order,” the show’s Instagram page posted a photo of Hargitay and Brunson on set and shared the following caption: “Two iconic New York Captains walk onto a set… 📸
Hargitay has spoken about her admiration of Brunson on several occasions, referring to him as a “friend” and calling him “my inspiration” in June while appearing on TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle.
“He is so singular and magnificent. He’s a magnificent human,” she said.

title: ‘The Traitors: New Blood’ Episode 9 Recap: Death By Poisoned Chalice
summary: Read a recap of “The Traitors: New Blood” Episode 9 to find out who survived the Highland Feast and how many Traitors are still in the turret as the end of the game approaches.
story: Warning: Spoilers from “The Traitors: New Blood” Episode 9 below.
One Faithful has spent their last night in the castle after unknowingly drinking from a poisoned chalice, eliminating them from the game.

In Episode 9 of “The Traitors: New Blood,” which aired Nov. 5, the remaining players put on their fanciest clothes to attend Alan Cumming’s Highland Feast, a celebration after successfully banishing their first Traitor of the season.

But the party wasn’t just an opportunity for the players to bond. Prior to the gathering, the Traitors were secretly informed that they had to poison a Faithful’s chalice and murder them. With the Traitors down a member, they needed to remove the correct player from the game in order to regain the upper hand and paint a target on a Faithful.
Read on to find out who survived the Highland Feast and how many Traitors are still in the turret as the end of the game approaches.
The Highland Feast Brings Tears and Chaos

Episode 9, titled “Playing Chess,” opens with the players gathering around a table for a seemingly more pleasant evening. Some of the players become emotional as they share what the game has meant to them. Ben says he finally feels like “one of the boys” after forming strong connections with the men and Abbey B. reveals she is grateful for the experience because her home life has been “isolating” while she cares for her daughter. Shane also opens up about the death of his sister and how it has impacted his family.

Alan interrupts the heartfelt conversation as the episode rewinds to two hours earlier. Traitors Katie and Joe are shown entering the confessional room where they receive a note that reads, “Traitors, tonight after the dinner someone will be poisoned. Whilst everyone is getting ready for dinner, you must sneak down and meet in the secret room to decide who you want to murder by assigning that player a poisoned chalice.”

But there was an additional twist. “Each player must drink, however, they do not have to drink their own glass,” the message said. “They can discuss and drink someone else’s glass instead. If a Traitor ends up drinking from the poisoned chalice, there will be no murder tonight.”

Katie and Joe begin to strategize. He worries he is in a “dead man walking situation” following Tomica’s banishment and Victor publicly declaring that he would target Joe next. Joe says he needs “to do something drastic” to save himself and suggests poisoning Victor. But Katie reminds him that Victor might switch his drink with someone else and disrupt their plans.

Back at the Highland Feast, the players join Alan outside and he reveals one of them will be murdered after drinking from a poisoned glass. He tells them they have two minutes until he makes his toast — whichever glass they are holding when he begins his speech will be the one they drink from.

Victor is immediately anxious and wants a player to switch drinks with him. He asks Joe, who declines. Kriste is also disinterested in changing her glass which makes Ben suspicious. Before time runs out, Shane and Joe swap drinks. In his confessional, Joe confirms that the Traitors pulled off the murder. “Today, we’re back in the win column,” he says.
A Murder and a Spirited Challenge With a Hidden Shield

At breakfast, multiple players start sharing their theories. Abbey B. questions why Joe didn’t want to switch with Victor while Jay says he still suspects Victor is a Traitor. Shane is suspicious of Joe, as well, but Ben is focused on Katie and Kriste.

The players arrive in groups until it is revealed that Morgan was murdered. “They gave me the poisoned chalice!” Morgan says when she learns she was killed. After reading the note from the Traitors, she tells the camera, “And that kids is why you do not drink something you didn’t pour yourself at parties.”
She continues, “Shoot! This was the hardest thing I’ve ever done. But also the coolest thing. I wouldn’t change anything other than swap my glass. That’s for sure.”
The Faithfuls are confused by Morgan’s murder. They briefly discuss her departure before Alan strolls into the Breakfast Room and tells them, “Keep your spirits up.”

The players meet Alan at his creepy cabin in the woods. For the mission, they have to enter the shack and summon a spirit. The spirit will call them and name an item they want to be reunited with. The players must find the correct item and hand it over. If they answer correctly, they will receive $9,000 per item. If they are wrong, the player who delivers the item will be dragged from the cabin. There is also a shield up for grabs.

The players work together to give the spirit the right bottle of beer in round one. But during round two, they fail to find the exact wedding dress and Jay is eliminated. In between rounds, Victor finds a shield and quickly stows it away without anyone seeing. For the final round, Abbey B. braves a smelly bathroom to grab the last item, adding $18,000 in total to the prize pot.
The Traitors Prepare to Battle

Going into the Round Table, Katie says she is aware Joe’s name is being thrown out. But, she wants to try to save him and keep the Traitors in power. During the day, she mentioned Wyatt and Kriste to other players, hoping to point them in the wrong direction.

However, her tactic did not work on Victor. He says in his confessional that he is certain Joe is a Traitor and he will work hard at the Round Table to get everyone on his side. He says he will not back down and will try to stop the players from voting for Kriste.
Joe is also ready to fight for survival. “It’s me versus Victor, and I’m going to come out on top,” he says as the episode ends.
What Will Happen Next Week?

Episode 10, “The Sun, the Moon and the Truth,” will show Victor and Joe going head-to-head at the Round Table. If Joe survives, the Traitors will have a better chance of winning the game. But if he is banished, Katie will be left alone in the turret.
The next episode will be released on Thursday, Nov. 12, at 8 p.m. PT/ET and 7 p.m. CT on NBC. The episode will also stream the next day on Peacock.
In just two weeks, the season will conclude in an epic two-hour finale on Thursday, Nov. 19.

title: Aaron Carter’s Ex Shares Update on Their Son on Anniversary of His Death
summary: The late Aaron Carter’s ex, Melanie Martin, shared a heartfelt tribute, including an update on their son Prince, on the four-year anniversary of the singer’s death.
story: It’s been four year since Aaron Carter died, and his fiancée is honoring her late love, while also sharing an update on their son, Princeton Lyrik Carter.
In an Instagram post shared Nov. 5, Melanie Martin first reflected on the day that forever changed her life.

“Some days it feels like yesterday, and other days it feels like a lifetime ago. I still wish I could hear your voice, tell you about our day, or have just one more conversation with you,” she wrote, adding that she missed the man she know “behind closed doors.”
“You were so much more than the headlines or the struggles people saw. I wish the world had shown you more kindness and compassion,” she added.
Amid her grief, she shared some insight on now-4-year-old Princeton.
“The hardest part is watching Prince grow up without you,” Martin wrote. “He’s learning so much and becoming his own little person.”
She added that she wishes the “I Want Candy” singer “could see every milestone. I promise he will always know how much his daddy was loved.”
She continued to share how Carter’s death taught her the importance of mental health and the need to get proper care.

“You never know what someone is silently fighting,” she wrote, later adding, “Grief doesn’t have an expiration date. I can smile, make memories, and keep going for our son while still missing you every day. Both things can be true.”
She concluded by reminding people to check on their loved ones and be gentle with those who are struggling.
“A little compassion can mean more than you realize. I wish our story had a different ending,” she wrote. “I wish you had more time. Forever in my heart, Aaron.”

Martin has shared photos and videos of Prince over the years. Most recently she posted their Harley Quinn and Joker Halloween costumes. The young boy was seen sporting his late dad’s signature haircut from when he was a rising star.
Carter’s twin sister Angel Carter Conrad also shared a tribute on her Instagram story, expressing how much she misses him.
“I love that you still find ways to visit me in my dreams, especially during life’s biggest moments,” she wrote, adding how she will also continue to honor his memory.
Carter was found dead in his Lancaster, California, home on Nov. 5, 2022, at the age of 34. He had struggled with addiction and mental health issues over his lifetime.

The teen idol died by accidental drowning in his bathtub after inhaling difluoroethane and taking alprazolam, the generic form of Xanax, according to a Los Angeles County Department of Medical Examiner-Coroner report.

title: Lauren Speed-Hamilton to Host a New YouTube Series, ‘Pull Up.’ See the Trailer
summary: Reality television star Lauren Speed-Hamilton is prepared to push her guests outside of their comfort zones in her new celebrity interview series. Watch the exclusive trailer.
story: Reality television star Lauren Speed-Hamilton is prepared to push her guests outside of their comfort zones in her new celebrity interview series.
TODAY.com can exclusively reveal that the “Love Is Blind” alum, who found love on Season 1 of the Netflix dating show, will host “Pull Up,” premiering on YouTube Thursday, Nov. 12.

For the first season, Speed-Hamilton, will be joined by “The Real Housewives of Atlanta” star Cynthia Bailey, comedian KevOnStage, husband Cameron Hamilton and more guests for candid conversations in unexpected places. Speed-Hamilton will stop by the recording studio to chat with some guests, put her strength to the test in an aerial class with another and challenge her husband to an axe throwing contest when they meet up.
In a trailer for the series, exclusively shared by TODAY.com, Speed-Hamilton introduces the show by asking, “Who wants beef? I’m ready.”
Later when she interviews her husband, she jokes, “Is Cam trying to leave me on this show?”
After revealing the other three guests who will appear in Season 1, she says, “Crazy, right? But we’re going to get into it all.”
See the full trailer below.
Prior to the trailer release, Speed-Hamilton teased the new project on her Instagram story Nov. 4. She shared with fans that she is the creator and executive producer of “Pull Up.”

“This show has been such a labor of love,” she said. “First off, what possessed me to create a huge project like this in my first year of motherhood? I don’t know. But we did it y’all. And it turned out so amazing, so great, and I’m so proud of it. I’m really excited for y’all to see it.”

“Pull Up” will be available to watch on the couple’s “Hanging With The Hamiltons” YouTube channel. The two previously had a podcast they released on their channel called “The Love Seat” where they spoke about love and relationships, including with fellow “Love Is Blind” stars Brett and Tiffany Brown and Amber Pike and Matt Barnett.
Recently they have been posting videos about entering a new chapter as first-time parents after welcoming their son, Ezra William Hamilton, in October 2025.
They shared a joint post on Instagram Nov. 1 celebrating Ezra’s first year. In the adorable clip, Speed-Hamilton cradled her newborn and said, “I’m your mommy.”
The clip showed the parents bonding with their baby boy and sharing sweet moments with him every month of the past year as Ezra learned to take his first steps.

title: Al Roker Inducts Scarlett Johansson into Very Special ‘5-Timer’s Club’
summary: Scarlett Johansson has hosted TODAY weather with Al Roker five times which means he is in the five timer’s club.
story: If the whole acting thing doesn’t work out for Scarlett Johansson, she can always fall back on another one of her skills: forecasting the weather.

While stopping by Studio 1A to discuss her new film “Paper Tiger,” the star marked a special milestone with TODAY’s resident weatherman, Al Roker, and helped him share the forecast for the fifth time live on TODAY.
“This is your fifth time. So much like they do on ‘SNL,’ we got you your fifth weather robe,” Al said as he helped the star put the robe on.
“Five-timers club!” Savannah said.

On “Saturday Night Live,” celebrities who host the show five times are typically presented with a special velvet jacket with the number five on it. Johansson is one of many stars who have received the honor.
The actor was touched by the gesture and hugged Al, saying, “This is a dream.”
“And we even have a little thunderbolt on the back for you,” Al pointed out.
“How chic,” the star said. “Oh my God, can I wear this out? It’s like a little dinner robe.”
As she approached the weather map, Johansson was impressed by how much activity was going on across the country.
“My gosh, you guys, look at all this. It looks like there’s a bunch of rain happening over here here along the coast,” she said.
As she examined the map, the actor pointed out one state that’s currently having gorgeous weather.
“Florida is where you want to be right now. That looks nice and roasty toasty,” she said.
As she made her way to the west coast, Johansson was surprised to see weather in the 30s in the Western Plains.
“What’s that all about?” she asked Al.
“It’s about fall,” he quipped.
Al and Johansson then highlighted some more rain on the east coast and the weatherman acknowledged that it’s been pretty dry lately.
“We’re so happy that there’s rain out there,” the actor said.
And just like that, the segment was over, and Al took a moment to congratulate the star.
“This was the best fifth weather ever!” he said.
“Yay!” Johansson exclaimed as she raised her arms in the air.

title: Met Gala Announces New 2027 Theme After Original Exhibit Was Canceled Amid Controversy
summary: The Metropolitan Museum of Art has announced its new theme for the 2027 Met Gala after scrapping its originally planned exhibition around British designer John Galliano.
story: The Metropolitan Museum of Art has announced its new theme for the 2027 Met Gala after scrapping its originally planned exhibition around British designer John Galliano.

The new theme for the gala and the Costume Institute’s spring exhibit revolves around jeans and T-shirts and is called “extraORDINARY: Fashion and the Poetics of the Everyday,” according to a Nov. 5 news release.

The exhibit will be “devoted to the undersung beauty and allure of quotidian garments—think the aforementioned t-shirts and jeans, plus raincoats, sweatshirts, puffer jackets, and more,” according to an announcement from Vogue.
The gala will explore how designers have reinvented everyday wear for the runway and used materials like paper, aluminum and plastic, “inviting visitors to see them anew.”
The 2027 Met Gala is being organized by curator in charge Andrew Bolton, who previously said he supported the decision not to go forward with the Galliano theme.

“It was really important to come up with an exhibition that wasn’t just a masterwork show or something that we could do a little bit more easily,” Bolton told Vogue. “That was really important to me: to come up with an idea that wasn’t a substitute. And it had to have some sort of contemporary resonance.”
The new theme comes just over two months after the Metropolitan Museum of Art announced that it was abandoning its planned theme around Galliano’s work, titled “John Galliano: Horizons.”

The theme faced a wave of criticism related to anti-Semitic and racist comments Galliano made in 2010 and 2011, some of which were captured on video. He was castigated for making comments about Jewish and Asian people on two separate occasions at the same Paris bar. He was fired as Dior’s creative director in the aftermath of the comments.
He said in court his remarks were made due to drug and alcohol addiction. Galliano has said that he is now sober.
Bolton issued a statement after the Met Gala scrapped the idea of a Galliano-themed event.
“I believe deeply in the responsibility of museums to examine difficult histories with rigor, candor, and care,” Bolton said.

“I also recognize the pain and concern this exhibition has caused,” he added. “After extensive discussion, I support the decision not to proceed. I remain deeply grateful to my colleagues and to the advisors, lenders, collaborators, and community leaders who contributed their knowledge, trust, and perspectives to the project.”

title: Parents, sister of far-right Kraków shooter found dead in family home
summary: Three bodies found in the home of the 24-year-old shooter in Saturday’s rampage in the heart of Kraków, Poland, belonged to the gunman’s family, police said.
story: Three bodies found in the home of the 24-year-old shooter in Saturday’s rampage in the heart of Kraków, Poland, belonged to the gunman’s family, police said.

Investigators are looking at the deaths of the shooter’s parents and sister as they unravel events surrounding the random violence in the Polish city’s historic center, Main Market Square, around 3 p.m. Saturday.
The relatives, who lived about 90 miles from Kraków, most likely died from gunshot wounds, according to police.
Authorities said the shooter, who survived a shootout with police and remains in the hospital, wore a bulletproof vest.

World leaders paid tribute to victims, and Poland declared two national days of mourning after the shooter, motivated by far-right ideologies killed six people in Kraków in what the country’s defense minister characterized as a “terror attack.”

The dead are a man from the United Kingdom, a woman from Austria and four Polish nationals, according to regional official Krzysztof Jan Klęczar. The injured include visitors from Britain, Portugal, Russia, Germany and Austria, according to The Associated Press.
St. Mary’s Basilica in the square paused its hourly trumpet call overnight in honor of the victims. It was the first time the historic church had done so since World War II.

The gunman, whom officials described as having “ultranationalistic” beliefs, is reported to have opened fire in Kraków’s Main Market Square. The midday attack was the country’s deadliest shooting in decades, while a policeman who confronted the gunman is in critical condition.

The suspect is being investigated on suspicion of murder in connection, Justice Minister Waldemar Żurek said Sunday on X, adding that he “acted with the aim of seriously intimidating a large number of people, making this a terrorist offence.”
The same suspect faces a separate murder charge over killings in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyskie, Żurek said, a town 93 miles northeast of Kraków, where three of his relatives were found dead in his home.

“Establishing all the circumstances of these tragic events, determining the full sequence of the perpetrator’s actions and securing evidence are currently the priorities of the investigation,” which is being led by terror offense specialists within the prosecutor’s office, he said.
Kraków prosecutor Eryk Stasielak said that the shooter was in critical condition and that victim autopsies are set to start Monday, according to PAP, a Polish news service.
“Tomorrow we will be deciding the fate of the attacker, if he survives, because he remains in critical condition,” Stasielak said, according to a translation of the report.

Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński did not name the suspect, identifying him only as a Polish national in his mid-20s from Ostrowiec Świętokrzyskie. He used an automatic rifle, Kierwiński said Saturday, describing him as having “ultranationalistic” views.
“Everything indicates he was fascinated by far-right ideologies,” he said.
The suspect was shot by police at the scene and taken to the hospital around 3 p.m.
A man and two women later found dead in an apartment are believed to be the suspect’s parents and sister, according to Andrzej Fijołek, deputy inspector of Police National Headquarters.
The Interior Ministry announced two national days of mourning Sunday and Monday.

Pope Leo XIV expressed his sadness in a message to the archbishop of Kraków on Sunday. The pope “implores the gift of Christian hope for the families overwhelmed by grief and joins with all those experiencing these days of mourning,” the message read, according to a translation.
Żurek, the justice minister, said early Sunday on social media that Senior Constable Jakub Kulik “is fighting for his life in hospital” after he confronted the shooter.
“One of his lungs is not functioning, and he needs every drop of blood he can get,” he posted on X.
Police later said blood banks in Kraków were full and thanked those who donated.
“Senior constable Jakub Kulik and senior constable Artur Moranski are true heroes,” Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said, referring to both officers.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Klęczar said that without “the efficient and selfless intervention” of the officers, “the number of victims could have been significantly higher.”
“The condition of the two police officers remains serious,” Klęczar said Sunday. Kierwiński later said the two men had been brought out of comas.

Video on social media shows what appears to be an injured police officer firing at the gunman before he drops to his knees and rolls over onto his back. The officer, who did not appear to have backup nearby, struggles to reload his firearm and appears to be clutching his right arm.
British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said the U.K. government “deeply mourns the British national and other victims” who died.
“The U.K. stands resolutely in solidarity with the people of Poland,” he said.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy also said Saturday that his country “stands in solidarity” with neighboring Poland, calling the shooting a “shocking crime.”
The U.S. State Department said it was not aware of any American citizens harmed in the violence.
“The profound depth of Poland’s shock at the horror of yesterday’s appalling mass murder in Krakow is truly remarkable to behold,” the U.S. ambassador to Poland, Tom Rose, said in a post on X.

Noting how rare the incident was in an “extraordinarily safe” country like Poland, he added, “There’s something profoundly precious about being in a country where such evil remains so foreign to everyday life, where an entire nation recoils in horror at the mere thought of it, and where the depth of grief reveals the true goodness of its people.”
Part of Main Market Square in Kraków and surrounding streets reopened Sunday, but cordons remain while police carry out forensic work, the city has said in a statement.
Several makeshift memorials with flowers and candles appeared across the city Sunday.
Tourists caught up in attack
Many of those caught up in the attack were tourists visiting the city.

Taylor Dorfmeister, 21, a student from Santa Cruz, California, studying in Italy who was visiting Poland, was in the square with his roommate when gunfire erupted. Dorfmeister said there was a delay before the crowd reacted and then everyone began to flee. He said he took shelter in a building.
“We ran up the stairs in the building to hide, and it was a dead end, which is when I was the most terrified, since the gunshots were [loud] and near,” Dorfmeister told NBC News.
It sounded to Dorfmeister like the gunfire was coming from the first floor of the building where he hid. He was “fully prepared for the worst” based on the proximity of the noise, he said.
“This is it,” Dorfmeister thought. “Like, there’s nowhere to go, nowhere to hide.”
Marie-Ange Collaer was visiting with her family from Brussels.

“We literally ran for our lives and managed to hide from the bullets flying around,” she wrote on Facebook. “Lying on the floor in a shop like in a bad police movie whilst you hear bullets everywhere.”
Collaer said that her family were shaky and “quite in shock” after they returned to their hotel and that everyone was grateful to be alive.
“We saw a few that did not make it, true horror,” she wrote.
U.K. resident Neil Thaxton and his wife, Nicky, also survived the attack.

“We had just walked through the main square and heard the gunshots,” Thaxton wrote on Facebook. “We thought it was fireworks then people started running, we went into a gift shop and the staff took us in the back of the shop and locked the doors and turned the lights off.”

title: Gunman kills 6 in ‘terror attack’ in Poland, officials say; 3 others found dead in his home
summary: A gunman described as having “ultranationalistic” beliefs fatally shot six people while driving through a public square Saturday in Krakow, Poland, officials said, in what the country’s defense minister characterized as a “terror attack.” Three of his relatives were later found dead in his home.
story: A gunman described as having “ultranationalistic” beliefs fatally shot six people while driving through a public square Saturday in Kraków, Poland, officials said, in what the country’s defense minister characterized as a “terror attack.” Three of his relatives were later found dead in his home.

The relatives were found after the shooter opened fire in Kraków’s Main Market Square, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said. Four women and two men were killed in the midday attack in the city’s popular commerce and tourist destination, police said.

Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński identified the shooter as a man in his mid-20s from Ostrowiec Świętokrzyskie, a city some 93 miles northeast of Kraków. He used an automatic rifle, Kierwiński said, describing him as having “ultranationalistic” views.
“Everything indicates he was fascinated by far-right ideologies,” he said.
The shooter’s relatives, a man and two women found in an apartment, are believed to be his parents and sister, according to Andrzej Fijołek, deputy inspector of Police National Headquarters.
“We have the next acts of this tragedy,” Tusk said, describing the discovery of the bodies.
The discovery added another layer to the investigation into the attack at the square, which also left at least 15 people injured.
Two police officers were seriously wounded in the shooting, officials said. Tusk named the officers and described them as acting selflessly as the sound of gunfire sent market crowds running.

“Senior constable Jakub Kulik and senior constable Artur Moranski are true heroes,” the prime minister said. “They likely saved lots of lives while risking their own lives. Their conditions are serious but they are in good hands. All of Poland has their fingers crossed for you.”
One of the officers was was described earlier as undergoing surgery. He was shot three times, according to an earlier statement from Kierwiński.

The attacker, a Polish national, was shot by police at the scene and taken to the hospital around 3 p.m. local time. The shots were fired from a vehicle moving through the area, Kraków officials said in a series of posts on X.

An earlier post from the city’s official municipal government account said that investigators were working to determine the scale of the incident. The city announced a mourning period in recognition of the tragedy through Nov. 11.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Four of the dead in the city center attack have been identified, though their names were not released, Polish authorities said. They include three Polish nationals and a foreigner from the U.K., Kraków police and the U.K. Foreign Secretary said.
An Interior ⁠Ministry spokesperson said foreign nationals from Austria, ‌Germany, Portugal, ‌Russia and Britain are among the injured.⁠
The U.S. State Department said it was not aware of any American citizens harmed in the violence.

Katarzyna Cisło, a spokesperson for the Kraków police, told TVN24 that the gunman was wearing military-style fatigues and used a military-type long gun in the attack. Police found other weapons, as well as ammunition, in his car.

Video posted on social media shows what appears to be an injured police officer firing at the gunman before dropping to his knees and rolling over onto his back. The officer, who did not appear to have backup nearby, is seen struggling to reload his firearm and appeared to be clutching his right arm.

It was unclear whether the officer seen in the video is the same one mentioned in the interior minister’s update. Małopolska Police wrote in an X post that no officer had been killed, citing what they said were incorrect reports.
Other chilling video clips taken from the scene show a black car racing through the square. Dozens of people begin running in various directions at the sound of gunfire.

Police exchanged gunfire with the attacker as he went on a “wild ride” through the square, which is why victims were found in various locations, police officials said. The shooter continued to fire at officers after he was struck, but he was ultimately subdued, they said.
Some social media clips show responders attempting lifesaving measures on victims. Lifeless bodies could be seen scattered around the streets after the attack.

Taylor Dorfmeister, a 21-year-old American student studying in Italy who was visiting Poland, was in the square with his roommate when gunfire erupted. Dorfmeister said there was a delay before the crowd reacted and then everyone began to flee the area. He said he took shelter in a building.
“We ran up the stairs in the building to hide and it was a dead end, which is when I was the most terrified since the gunshots were [loud] and near,” Dorfmeister told NBC News.

It sounded to Dorfmeister like the gunfire was coming from the first floor of the building where he hid. The student from Santa Cruz, California, was “fully prepared for the worst” based on the proximity of the noise, he said.
“This is it,” Dorfmeister thought. “Like, there’s nowhere to go, nowhere to hide.”

“We are just learning details of the horrific mass shooting in Kraków, a savage and murderous attack that’s shattered the peace of Poland,” Tom Rose, the U.S. ambassador to Poland, wrote on X. “America stands with Poland at this dark hour as Poland stands with her beloved citizens of Kraków.”

The Main Market Square sits at the heart of Kraków’s medieval Old Town, where centuries of trade transpired under changing political and religious influences. Laid out in 1257, the sprawling plaza is home to the historic Cloth Hall and St. Mary’s Basilica.
It is considered the largest market square in Europe with history preserved in historical homes, houses of worship and ornate palaces, according to the UNESCO World Heritage Convention.
Mansions throughout the square were home to Polish royalty and aristocrats. It was renamed for Adolf Hitler and served as a Nazi propaganda base during the World War II occupation of Poland.

title: Pope Leo, who had cancer surgery weeks ago, begins South American tour
summary: Less than a month after Pope Leo XIV underwent cancer surgery, he set off on what the Vatican called a “homecoming” tour of South America.
story: ABOARD THE PAPAL FLIGHT — Three countries in 12 days, a dozen flights, two helicopter rides and nine Masses on a trip covering around 19,000 miles. Less than a month after Pope Leo XIV underwent cancer surgery, he set off on what the Vatican called a “homecoming” tour of South America.
The 71-year-old’s long trip across the strongly Catholic region will take him to Uruguay and Argentina, as well as to Peru, where he lived for decades and served as a bishop until 2023.

Leo considers the tour, one of the most grueling undertaken by a Catholic leader in decades, a “homecoming to places where he spent a long time and to which he feels closely connected,” Vatican spokesperson Matteo Bruni told journalists at a briefing Tuesday.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

The Chicago-born pontiff, who is also a citizen of Peru, told pilgrims at his weekly audience in St. Peter’s Square on Wednesday that he was ⁠hoping to “strengthen the faith, renew hope” and “rekindle the fire of charity.”
Leo will hold several meetings with survivors of sexual abuse by ​Catholic clergy during the trip, the Vatican has said, without yet providing further details.

Bruni said the pope would also address a range of issues facing the continent, including environmental destruction, ⁠arms trafficking and regional political instability, bringing “a message of communion and unity.”

title: Investors try to regain their footing after tech stocks tank
summary: Tech stocks in the U.S. steadied Friday after suffering one of their worst routs in years, as investors weighed the prospect of an AI investment slowdown.
story: Tech stocks in the U.S. steadied Friday after suffering one of their worst routs in years, as investors weighed the prospect of an AI investment slowdown resulting from Democratic midterm victories against the sector’s long-term growth potential.
The tech-focused Nasdaq 100 closed up 1.1% after plunging 6.3% on Thursday, its worst single-day performance since the Covid-19 pandemic.
The broader S&P 500 finished 0.3% higher, after tanking 4.4% Thursday, a drop that wiped out $2.8 trillion worth of wealth on paper.

A strong October jobs report Friday morning increased the odds that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates at its next policy meeting in December. The prospect of higher borrowing costs helped to push stocks down from their highs earlier in the day.

Investors continue to digest the results of Tuesday’s midterm elections, in which a crop of Democratic candidates were elected to office who had pledged to rein in AI and data centers. They include Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa of Texas, a state that is among the largest data center markets in the country.
The AI boom is responsible for an ever-increasing share of U.S. stock market gains and economic growth, so any threat to the narrative of demand-fueled growth can rattle investors.
“Markets are being punished according to their dependence on the U.S. AI infrastructure cycle,” Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Singapore-based SAXO Markets, told NBC News.
The incoming Democratic-controlled Congress could also tighten scrutiny of the AI industry, including its infrastructure projects, which could cause delays and additional costs.
This would add to existing worries investors already have about the long-term profitability of these investments.
Some analysts viewed Thursday’s dramatic sell-off as overblown —  merely a sign of some froth coming off an overstretched market —  rather than the end of the line for the AI investment boom.
Recent declines are “just speed bumps,” said economist and investor Ed Yardeni.
Rather than spelling doom for the sector, Yardeni said, losses like this week’s could ultimately help keep the AI bubble from overheating.
Until it becomes clearer how much data center construction is truly threatened by newly elected lawmakers, volatility is likely to continue.

“This is a stock market that is trying to figure out the right valuations for the AI trade, which is grappling with a swift sentiment shift after the midterm elections,” said Alex Guiliano, the chief investment officer at New Jersey-based Resonate Wealth Partners.

title: Wave of bomb threats against European airliners triggers diversions and tarmac searches
summary: No explosives have been found, and it isn’t clear who or what is behind the calls, but the threats alone have caused chaos in the skies and airports.
story: LONDON — A wave of bomb threats against passenger airliners caused chaos in the skies and airports of Europe on Thursday, the latest of such incidents this week that have prompted emergency landings and security sweeps on runways.

No explosives have so far been found, and it is not clear who or what is behind the security threats made against at least 14 airliners. But the threats have caused disruption to Europe’s airspace and some of its busiest airports.

The threats against two flights that landed in Rome came by email that cited opposition to “your feminist regime,” the airport confirmed to NBC News. Italy’s prime minister, Giorgia Meloni, is a woman who has conservative views.

One of the first reports involved Aer Lingus Flight EI402 from Dublin to Rome, which changed course near Paris and diverted to a French air force base, the airline said. There, all 151 passengers and six crewmembers were evacuated while a bomb squad inspected the aircraft, French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu’s office said in a statement.
Confirmed flights threatened Thursday

Aer Lingus EI402 from Dublin to Rome — received bomb threat over France, made emergency landing at air base and inspected by bomb squad, according to airline and French officials.Finnair AY1761 from Helsinki, Finland, to Rome Fiumicino — escorted into Rome by Italian air force jets, bomb squad search found no explosives, airline said.Finnair AY1471 from Helsinki to Vienna — also received bomb threat, likewise no explosives found, according to airline.LOT Polish Airlines LO235 from Warsaw, Poland, to Brussels — crew made midair checks after receiving threat, "additional screening" once in Brussels found no "suspicious items," airline said.LOT Polish Airlines LO331 from Warsaw to Paris — stopped while taxiing and directed to parking stand where searched, airline said. Passengers continued on trips after switching planes.Ryanair FR3606 from Copenhagen, Denmark, to Sofia, Bulgaria, and Ryanair FR6410 from Madrid to Sofia — both landed normally following bomb threat, no explosives found, according to Bulgarian Transport Ministry.Ryanair FR1730 from London Stansted to Sofia — also received a bomb threat and diverted to Plovdiv, Bulgaria, the Bulgarian Transport Ministry said.Wizz Air WMT3064 from Milan to Bucharest — airport said it was notified of the bomb threat as flight was arriving, bomb squad found nothing.Czech police say four unidentified flights headed for Prague also received threats.
Aer Lingus EI402 from Dublin to Rome — received bomb threat over France, made emergency landing at air base and inspected by bomb squad, according to airline and French officials.
